plan.summary: This 1-4 block fits a 12-week off-camp boxing strength-and-power plan with very low lifting frequency to leave room for sparring and skill work. Week 1 establishes a simple baseline with a bodyweight lower-body strength assessment so later weeks can be progressed clearly, and the main training work starts in Week 2. Because equipment is limited to bodyweight only and you train S&C once per week, the block emphasizes safe explosive jumps, unilateral leg strength, push-up strength, trunk work, and short low-cost conditioning.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic lower-body strength, simple explosive ability, and trunk control with low-equipment work that does not clash with sparring.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress unilateral strength and power output while keeping weekly fatigue low enough to support boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength topped up and shift more of the session toward faster, sharper explosive efforts.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Reset between reps. Jump as high and fast as possible and land softly.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if repeated countermovement timing feels inconsistent. Start from a still quarter squat and jump hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jumps
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if jumping height is limited today. Keep contacts light and springy.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: This session establishes your baseline for future progress. Warm up with easy sets on each leg, then build to one hard set of 3-5 clean reps per side using a slow lower and full range. If bodyweight is too easy, use a 3-4 second lowering phase and a 2 second pause at the bottom.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to one hardest clean set of 3-5 reps per side. Log reps, tempo used, and whether the set was bodyweight only so the app can track your baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Beat this baseline over time with cleaner reps, more control, or added difficulty before adding more total volume.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rear-foot-elevated setup is awkward. Keep the front foot flat and reach full depth.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a stable box or stair if split squats bother the hips. Drive through the whole foot and control the descent.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave 1-2 good reps in reserve on every set. Body stays straight and chest reaches full depth.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a bench, box, or sturdy surface if full push-ups are not yet clean for all reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3 second lowering phase if regular push-ups are too easy.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Step back under control and drive up smoothly. Keep the front knee tracking over the foot.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if balance is a limiting factor. Stay tall and control the bottom.

substitutionOptions.name: Walking Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space allows and knees feel good. Keep stride length consistent.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep the lower back gently pressed down and ribs tucked. Stop before position breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow hold is too difficult to keep clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Tuck Hollow Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Shorten the lever if full hollow position cannot be held well.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, squeeze glutes, and keep the body in one straight line.

substitutionOptions.name: RKC Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use shorter harder efforts if standard planks are too easy.

substitutionOptions.name: Bear Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if shoulder comfort is better in a bent-knee position.

exercises.name: Shadowboxing Tempo Intervals
exercises.notes: Move lightly and stay crisp. Keep the effort controlled so you finish fresher, not flatter.

endurancePrescription.format: 6 rounds of 1 minute on, 1 minute easy movement
